rationale: Evidence from iteration 7 (score 531.0, best so far, up from 417.0): body_length 0.14 to 0.10 cut the s-bend off-track rate. The oval still finishes 20/20 (steering_oscillation 0.14), s-bend progress rose from 0.57 to 0.91 with 7/20 finishes, and the slalom is still 0/20 (progress 0.23, one line-loss event per run). The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), which is 0.06 m for every allowed body width. Lag on bends is the failure mode, not lost tape. Yaw inertia is mass*(L^2+W^2)/12, and body_length is now at its 0.10 minimum, so body_width is the remaining lever. Changing body_width from 0.12 to 0.08 cuts L^2+W^2 from 0.0244 to 0.0164, a 33 percent reduction in yaw inertia. Its only other effect is the off-track limit, which stays at 0.06 m because 0.0125 + 0.08/4 = 0.0325 is below it. So this change should make the robot turn faster on bends at no cost in the limit. I am changing only body_width, keeping kp 5.0, kd 1.2, base_speed 1.1, sensors and mass fixed, so the effect can be read directly. Expected result: s-bend progress above 0.95 with more finishes, slalom progress rising toward 0.3 or more, and the oval staying at 100 percent with steering_oscillation at or below about 0.2. Hypotheses: (H1) yaw inertia is the main bend-lag term, so the bend tracks improve further. (H2) if oval oscillation rises above 0.2, the faster yaw response is overshooting and kd should go to about 1.5. (H3) if the slalom does not move, its limit is sensor coverage or response speed on alternating curves, which points to a 7-sensor array inside x = ±0.07 m or a lower base_speed with a higher kp.
